## You must change `tests/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [tests/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
The check the audit contract prescribes is `git -C redblue log --oneline main | grep checkpoint`, and phase-078's finding cites eight commits on that basis: 7fdea15, 074c95e, 563a351, 286fccd (`rbops: phase-0NN checkpoint`) and the merges e97983a, d664d3c, 2179034, 255816e. Measured this audit, NONE of them reproduces: `git -C redblue log --oneline main | grep -c checkpoint` prints 0, and `git -C redblue merge-base --is-ancestor <c> main` returns false for all eight. A check written to that finding would scan an empty set and pass vacuously. The same defect is on main THIRTEEN times under a different subject - `git -C redblue log --oneline main | grep 'resume phase'` prints 09dd102, 985e445, 96c3c17, 8910456, 1ee5aba, b6d633b, dff04f6, 4c45731, 11b9fe2, 2804ab8, 861080d, 25e9b68 and 825193a, each titled `resume phase-NNN: adopt preserved work`, together 27,984 changed lines (`git show --stat` summed per commit; 09dd102 alone is 35 files / 1437 insertions). phase-051 and phase-079 are a different defect (work in the working tree, not ancestry) and do not cover this. This phase SUPERSEDES phase-078's finding, which is provably false as written.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Install an executable check that fails when a commit carrying unreviewed work is an ancestor of redblue main and is not on a written acknowledgement list, matching the commit subjects the pipeline actually writes.

## Method

1. Read `AGENTS.md` in full. Obey every hard rule; they are not negotiable.
2. Reproduce the finding. Record the exact command and the exact wrong output.
3. Write the failing test FIRST. Watch it fail. Do not touch production code
   until you have a red test that fails for the right reason.
4. Make the smallest change that turns it green.
5. Run the four gates yourself before claiming anything:

   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   cargo test --all-targets
   ./rbops/verify.sh phase-083
   ```

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] a test runs `git log --format=%H%x09%s` over HEAD and fails for ANY subject matching `checkpoint` OR `resume phase-` that is not named in an acknowledgement list inside the test file
- [ ] the acknowledgement list names all thirteen `resume phase-NNN: adopt preserved work` commits measured at audit time - 09dd102, 985e445, 96c3c17, 8910456, 1ee5aba, b6d633b, dff04f6, 4c45731, 11b9fe2, 2804ab8, 861080d, 25e9b68, 825193a - each with a line recording that it carries unreviewed code and was deliberately not rewritten
- [ ] a second test asserts phase-078's eight superseded commits (7fdea15, 074c95e, 563a351, 286fccd, e97983a, d664d3c, 2179034, 255816e) are NOT ancestors of HEAD, so the stale finding cannot be silently re-derived
- [ ] the tests are deterministic and offline: no network, no path outside the repository, no wall-clock, no dependence on reflog or stash state
- [ ] edge_* tests cover: a log with zero unreviewed commits, a log whose only unreviewed commits are acknowledged, a log with exactly one unacknowledged commit, a subject merely CONTAINING the word checkpoint inside a longer phrase, and a two-tab-delimited malformed subject line
- [ ] REPORT.md states that phase-078's finding was measured false and why, so the supersession is on the record
- [ ] `cargo test` reports 0 failures and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean with no `allow(` added and no `#[ignore]`
